title: ContentBlock
description: A piece of learning content with a canonical meaning and a bundle of representations - but NO chosen rendering. The Modality Router selects representations at runtime from the learner's Communication Ability Profile (ADR-0001). Content authors never decide how something looks, which is why no module can ship inaccessible.

id.description: Stable dotted identifier, e.g. 'phrase.clarify.repeat_request_01'. Never reused, never renamed - progress data references it.

canonical_text.description: The meaning, in plain standard English. This is the reference for scoring, never the thing rendered verbatim to every learner.

intent.description: The communicative function, e.g. 'request_clarification'. Drives scenario matching and the error signature used by the recommender.

scenario_tags.description: e.g. ['supervisor', 'shopfloor', 'first_week']. Used for RAG filtering in the role-play engine.

representations.description: One representation per channel. Missing entries trigger a documented fallback chain and a build-time CI warning - never a runtime surprise for a learner.

easy_read.description: Easy-Read paraphrase. Human-written, machine-linted: max 15 words per sentence, one clause per line.

caption.description: Caption text for the audio. Verbatim, not a paraphrase - captions that paraphrase are a documented failure for Deaf users.

phonemes.description: IPA phoneme sequence. G2P-generated, human spot-checked. Feeds forced alignment and GOP scoring (M6).

accepted_input_modes.description: Which input modes may answer this block. A block accepting only 'speech' excludes P2 and P4 and will fail contract validation unless a non-speech sibling exists.

distractors.description: Plausible wrong options for recognition exercises.

common_errors.description: Known learner errors, used to pre-write targeted coaching rather than generating it.

a11y.description: Asserted in CI. No ContentBlock may require a channel that a supported profile lacks unless an equivalent representation exists. This is the automated guarantee behind 'accessibility as architecture'.

source.description: 'generated' content is labelled as AI-generated to the learner until a trainer reviews it (Ethics E5).
